paragraphs.text: Many people start running with great enthusiasm but give up within a few weeks, often because they try to do too much too soon. Experts recommend beginning with a mix of walking and running rather than running continuously.

A typical beginner plan lasts nine weeks. In the first week, runners alternate one minute of jogging with ninety seconds of walking for twenty minutes, three times a week. The running periods gradually become longer until the runner can jog for thirty minutes without stopping.
Rest days are an important part of the plan, because muscles and joints need time to adapt. Beginners who run every day are more likely to suffer injuries, particularly to the knees and shins.
Good shoes matter more than expensive clothing. Many sports shops will watch customers run on a treadmill and recommend shoes that suit the way they move.
Running with a friend or joining a local group can also make it easier to keep going on days when motivation is low.
